title: Dedicated throughput entitlement, notification & crediting language
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: define a customer-facing, legally-ready wording and operational definition for Dedicated capacity throughput entitlements that ties SLA measurement windows to an error-budget driven autoscale policy, a customer notification and remediation cadence, and a transparent crediting model.

Goals: 1) Provide precise SLO definitions (units, percentiles, and windows) that can be measured automatically from the Dedicated telemetry pipeline; 2) Define an error-budget consumption metric that can be used to trigger autoscale actions and customer notices; 3) Specify credit calculation and accrual/decay rules for contractual remediation; 4) Add contract clauses for temporary throttling, regional failover (AZ-level degradation), and force majeure; 5) Surface a customer API and Console UX that shows current entitlement balance, recent incidents, and next remediation steps.

Key deliverables: human-readable contract paragraphs for Master Services Agreement (MSA) + two attachment examples (one for enterprise reserved pools, one for burstable reserved pools); measurement spec for telemetry team; autoscale-trigger mapping doc for runtime; sample Console/API payloads for entitlement queries; operational playbook for SEs/CS (what notices to send at each threshold).

Measurement summary (operational): Throughput entitlement will be expressed as Sustained RPS (requests per second) and Sustained TPU (tokens-per-second) per committed unit, measured with a 5-minute rolling window and aggregated into a 24-hour rolling SLO. Error budget is computed as the proportion of 5-minute windows in 24 hours where tail P95 latency exceeds the committed latency target OR effective throughput drops below 90% of committed baseline after autoscale attempts. Autoscale triggers are mapped to cumulative error-budget burn over 30 minutes and 6 hours (fast/slow burn policies). Credits are calculated weekly and applied as dollar-equivalent tokens; credits accrue in a customer-credit bucket and decay at a half-life of 90 days unless explicitly consumed in refunds or future billing offsets.

Contract excerpt (draft): "If Redwood fails to deliver the Sustained Throughput Entitlement for a calendar day due to platform degradation (excluding Force Majeure or Customer misconfiguration), Customer shall be eligible to receive a Service Credit equal to the lesser of (a) the pro-rata portion of the monthly fee attributable to the affected Dedicated Pool for the period of degradation; or (b) the dollar equivalent computed from the Credit Formula in Attachment A. Service Credits are subject to Customer submission of a notice within 30 days and shall be the sole and exclusive remedy. Temporary rate-limiting applied to protect other customer entitlements will not constitute a waiver of Customer credits; Redwood will provide prior notice where feasible and post-incident root cause and remediation ETA within the timelines in Section X." 

Boundary cases and examples are included in the attachments (sustained hardware failure, partial AZ degradation, noisy neighbor, scheduled maintenance misconfiguration).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Contract language drafted and reviewed by Legal and Sales; 2) Measurement spec approved by Observability/Telemetry and Runtime teams; 3) Autoscale-trigger mapping documented and reviewed by Runtime; 4) Console mock showing entitlement balance and incident timeline created and reviewed by DX; 5) Sample API response defined and a small internal test harness that simulates burn scenarios implemented; 6) At least one cross-team tabletop run-through executed and notes recorded.
comments: 2025-03-02 Marco Chen: Initial draft of measurement spec added. Mapped 5m rolling windows to 24h SLO. Need rhe runtime to confirm ability to emit P95 per-pool in current telemetry (assigned ENG-).

2025-03-03 Priya Rao (Legal): Reviewed contract excerpt; requested explicit notice window and a soft cap on cumulative credits per month to avoid unlimited liability — added clause to Attachment A to cap credits at the monthly committed fee. Legal asks for an SBOM for Private deployments before MSA signature (tracked separately).

2025-03-05 Elena Garcia (Runtime): Autoscale mapping looks feasible. Two implementation concerns: 1) autoscale cooldown after a hardware-triggered scale must be at least 10m; 2) cross-AZ failover will be handled as partial degradation rather than full outage — this changes how the error budget is applied. Filed ENG-19753 to track telemetry tags for AZ-level aggregation.

2025-03-07 Marcus Li (DX): Console mockups uploaded. Proposed UX: green/yellow/red entitlement tile, history sparkline, 'Request Credit' button that pre-fills incident window. Need product to confirm whether manual credit requests are allowed or fully automated.

2025-03-10 Aisha Patel: Incorporated legal cap language and runtime cooldown feedback. Added two example scenarios (noisy neighbor spike vs persistent throughput depression) and their resulting credit calculations. Ready for cross-team tabletop on 2025-03-12.

2025-03-12 Sophia Nguyen (Sales Ops): Noted that enterprise contracts sometimes require monthly credit statements; requested an opt-in mechanistic clause for monthly reconciliations. Also noted competition requests for dedicated exhaustion notifications via webhook — added to links as a delivery option for the API.
